In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the context of the Agda host, KIPLING is a type-safe dependently typed object calculus with a type-safe tagless interpreter.
this article shows how to represent the equality rules of a dependently typed language in its host, and how to use that equality to represent the language in a type-safe way.
, for the dependently typed language, the type-safe representation is a generic program, and the universe is the key.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have constructed a type-safe, type-indexed representation of KIPLING in which type equality is represented by the equality of the types of terms.
the universe is a universal solution to the problem of type-indexing.
we show that the type equality of an Agda term, when interpreted as the type of a KIPLING term, is equal to the Agda term.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a universe is not just a type-indexed type, it is a type-indexed universe of types.
type-safe representations are possible for dependently typed object languages, and they can be made to be type-safe with respect to the host's type equality.
the universe is not just a useful abstraction for generic programming - it is an indispensable tool for type-safe representation.
